# 3f Drift, unmanaged tags, router lifecycle, dashboard: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 3](./README.md#phase-3-routing), [router sync](../processes/routing/router-sync.md) (step 5 of adding, "preview, drift, unmanaged tags", "pausing and removing", rules), [router scripts → script generation](../processes/router-scripts/script-generation.md) (how Phase 4 will register routers), [RouterOS integration](../integrations/routeros.md), designs `RP-Router` ("Not Proxier's"), `RP-Routers`, `RP-Phone-router`, `RP-Dashboard-ok`, `RP-Main`, and the **As built** of 3e (the plan, the sync job, `routerostest`) and 1f/2c (dashboard areas, schedules that fan out per object).

**Done when:** every active router is checked for drift every `routing.drift_every` (read-only, against what Proxier applied) and, with `routing.drift_repair` on, repaired by a sync, otherwise notified with **Repair** on its page; tags Proxier never installed are kept per router with their entries, notified once per new set, and can be adopted (as the catalog's `v2fly:`/`iplist:` selector, as an existing service, or as a custom service made from the router's entries), removed from the router, or ignored; a router can be registered in **awaiting setup** (`routers.Register`, Phase 4's port wraps it), probed every 10 minutes for 7 days and activated with its initial sync on first contact; routers can be paused and resumed, and removed keeping or removing what Proxier installed; the routers list is complete; the dashboard has its Routing area; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Drift round | Schedule `routing.drift_round` (`Every: 6h`, `Setting: "routing.drift_every"`, jitter 10 min) enqueues the job of the same name (queue `routers`, step `enqueue`): one `routing.drift` per **active** router, `SkipIfBusy` on `router:<id>` (a router with a sync queued or running is skipped: that sync reads it anyway). | router-sync.md "Drift check (every 6 h, read-only)". |
| Drift check | `routing.drift` (queue `routers`, resource key `router:<id>`, 1 attempt, step `check`, `Quiet`): connect, read, then compare the router with the **applied** rows (not the desired state): a tag drifts when its DNS entries' `(name, exact)` hash differs from the applied hash, an entry isn't `FWD` to the forwarder, its address-list count differs, or it is gone. One `Write`: a sync row (`kind = drift`, the differing tags), the router's `drift` and `drift_checked_at`, the unmanaged tags (below). With drift and `routing.drift_repair` on: a sync (`trigger = drift`, no delay) and `routing.drift_detected{tags, repair: true}` (not notifying). With repair off: `routing.drift_detected{tags, repair: false}` (notifying) only when the set of drifting tags differs from the stored one, so the same drift notifies once; the router page shows **Repair** (a sync with `trigger = drift`). No drift: the stored set is cleared, nothing recorded. A check that can't connect fails its sync row only: no failure count, no event (a sync that needs the router reports it). | router-sync.md step 2 of "preview, drift…"; events.md "on only when auto-repair is off". |
| Unmanaged tags | Every read (sync, preview, drift check) updates `routing_router_unmanaged` in its transaction: tags on the router (DNS comments) that are neither applied nor desired, not empty and not `mtvpn:`, with their entry count, their names (at most 5 000, `{name, exact}`), `first_seen`, `last_seen`; rows for tags that are gone or now applied or desired are deleted. When the non-ignored unmanaged tags include one missing from `unmanaged_notified`: `routing.unmanaged_tags_found{tags: the new ones}` (notifying) and `unmanaged_notified` = the current set (a tag that leaves and comes back notifies again). | router-sync.md step 3; "once per new set". |
| Adopt | `GET /routing/routers/:id/unmanaged/:tag/adopt`: a page styled as a dialog offering, when they exist: **Adopt as v2fly:<tag>** (the catalog has that list), **Adopt as iplist:<spelled>** (the catalog has that site or group, spelled by 3c's rule), **Add <tag> to <list>** (a service with that tag exists), and always **Make a custom service from the router's 26 entries** (name and tag = the tag, rows from the stored names, origin `router`). Each adds the service to the router's list in one `Write` after the guard: a new upstream one through `lists.AddNew`, an existing one through `lists.Add`, a custom one through `lists.CheckSet` then `services.CreateCustomTx` and `lists.AddTx` (3g's pattern). The list is marked, so the next sync finds the entries desired (`record` or `update`). A tag that isn't a valid tag (`selector.ValidTag`) can't be adopted: the page says why and offers **Remove** and **Ignore** only. | router-sync.md step 3 "Adopt". |
| Remove from router | Strength 2 ("Remove netflix (26 entries) from Home? Proxier never installed it; it goes on the next sync, now."): a sync with `remove: [tag]`, no delay, `trigger = unmanaged`; the plan turns that tag into a `remove` while it is still unmanaged. The sync records it (`router_synced{removed}`). | "Remove from router (confirmation)". |
| Ignore | **Ignore**: `ignored_at`, `routing.unmanaged_tag_ignored{tag, ignored: true}`; the tag leaves reports and notifications and stays on the router. Ignored tags are listed collapsed ("Ignored · 1") with **Stop ignoring** (`ignored: false`). | "Ignore: hidden from reports, left on the router". |
| Register | `routers.Register(ctx, r Registration, by string) (Registered, error)`: a router in **awaiting setup** (`awaiting_until = now + 7 days`, `created_by = by`), with name, list and connection validated as Add router's; `routing.router_added{list, host, by}`. It returns the id and the names the router script must use (`routeros.Names`). No test runs and no notification is ever sent for it. Phase 4 wraps it as `RouterRegistrar` (its transaction shape is Phase 4's choice). | router-sync.md step 5; modules/routing.md "Ports". |
| Probe | Schedule `routing.probe_round` (`Every: 10m`) enqueues the job of the same name (queue `routers`, step `enqueue`): one `routing.probe` (queue `routers`, resource key `router:<id>`, 1 attempt, `Quiet`, `SkipIfBusy`, step `probe`) per awaiting router with `now < awaiting_until`. The probe connects with `JumpFirstContact: ConfirmFirstContact` (a jump host must already be pinned) and `FirstContact: PinOnFirstContact` for the router (nobody can confirm a fresh router's key; it is pinned with subject `router:<id>`), runs `CmdCheck`: success → one `Write`: `active`, `awaiting_until = NULL`, version, board, `connected_at`, `last_seen_at`, `routing.router_connected{version, board}`, the initial sync (`trigger = initial`); failure → nothing recorded (no failure count, no event): the page shows the probe job's last error. After `awaiting_until` it isn't probed: the page says "never connected" with **Test connection**, whose pass (the admin confirms both keys) activates it the same way. | router-sync.md step 5; Build README defaults. |
| sshx | `sshx.Target` gains `JumpFirstContact FirstContact`, used for the jump hop. Its zero value is `PinOnFirstContact`, so a caller that sets only `FirstContact` must set both (routers' `Connection.Target` sets both to `ConfirmFirstContact`; servers have no jump host). | The probe needs different rules per hop. |
| Pause / Resume | **Pause syncs** (no dialog): `paused`; queued `routing.sync`, `routing.preview` and `routing.drift` jobs of the router are cancelled (`jobs.CancelQueued`); a running one finishes; `routing.router_paused`. Paused routers get no sync, preview, drift check or probe, and marks skip them. **Resume**: `active`, `routing.router_resumed`, a full sync now (`trigger = resume`). | router-sync.md "pausing". |
| Remove | `GET /routing/routers/:id/remove`, a page styled as a dialog with two choices: **Keep everything on the router** (default): in one `Write` queued jobs cancelled, the row deleted (its applied tags, unmanaged tags, syncs and tests with it), `routing.router_removed{name, cleaned: false}`. **Remove every tag Proxier installed**: `removing`, queued jobs cancelled, then `routing.remove` (queue `routers`, resource key `router:<id>`, 4 attempts like a sync, steps `connect`, `remove`, `delete`): `remove` reads, plans with `Extra{RemoveAll: true}` (every applied tag on the router becomes a removal; infra pins, untagged and unmanaged entries stay), pushes and verifies like a sync; `delete` deletes the row and records `routing.router_removed{name, cleaned: true}`. Its failures are recorded like a sync's (`routing.router_sync_failed{…, manual: true}`, notifying when the job gives up); the router stays `removing` (no syncs) with **Retry** (`jobs.Retry`) and **Remove without cleaning** (the keep path). The known hosts stay pinned (Settings → SSH can forget them). | router-sync.md "removing". |
| Routers list | `RP-Routers` completed: state (active; awaiting setup with a ring marker and "never connected · trying every 10 min until 12 Oct" or "never connected"; paused in foam; removing), list, last sync, and **Watch**: "▲ drift: youtube" (gold), "▲ 1 unmanaged tag: old-work", or "none". Sorted: failing first, then drift and unmanaged, then by name. The nav's Routers item stays without a counter. | `RP-Routers`. |
| Router page | Adds: the **Not Proxier's** area ("found on the router · never deleted on its own"): each unmanaged tag with its entries, "seen since 3 Oct", the catalog hint ("the catalog has v2fly:netflix"), **Adopt…**, **Ignore**, **Remove from router…**; the untagged line ("3 entries without a comment. Left alone unless a desired tag includes their name."); the infra pins line ("4 entries commented mtvpn: (mtvpn:doh and others) belong to the router script. Never touched."); "Ignored · N". The drift band ("Drift found at 04:10: youtube has 10 entries fewer than Proxier installed." with **Repair** when repair is off). The Connection area shows "Drift check every 6 h · auto-repair on". Actions gain **Pause syncs** / **Resume**, **Remove…**. Awaiting: a band "Awaiting setup: Proxier tries to connect every 10 minutes until 12 Oct. Install Proxier's key on the router." with the key and **Test connection**. Paused: "Paused: changes wait until you resume." Removing: the removal job's steps and log. | `RP-Router`, `RP-Phone-router`. |
| Per-hop status | The user chose this design extra (`RP-Phone-router`). A connect failure's band shows one row per hop, from the failed sync row's `hop` and `error` and the tailnet node's state now: **tailnet node proxier** ("up · Proxier itself is on the tailnet", or "off"; only when the first hop uses the tailnet), **jump host parents-pi** (when there is one), **router 10.230.2.1**; the failing hop shows its problem ("offline · dial tcp parents-pi:22: no route to host", "refused Proxier's key", "host key changed"), the hops before it "up", the ones after it "not tried · reached only through parents-pi". `routers.Hops(r Router, s Sync, node tailnet.Status) []Hop`, pure. Shown on every width, first on a phone. | `RP-Phone-router`. |
| Phone | Under 760 px the router page puts the band (with its hops), **Test connection**, **Sync now** and **Pause syncs** first, then "Last known state" (installed tags and names from the applied rows, "matched Main at 14:48"; waiting: the queued sync's `why`), the connection and recent syncs. | ui/README phone flow "run a sync". |
| Dashboard | The root implements `DashboardDeclarer` (`routing/dashboard.go`, composing `Routers`, `Refresh.Waiting` and `Refresh.LastDigest`): area **Routing** (link "Routers →"), after Links: routers with a failing sync (name, "sync failed at connect · 3 min ago"), drift ("drift: youtube") or unmanaged tags ("1 unmanaged tag"), first; when none, each active router with its last sync ("synced 1 h ago"); awaiting ones with "awaiting setup"; then **Snapshots** ("None waiting for a decision." or each waiting one: "netflix · 61 % drop · Review"); then **Daily refresh** from the last digest ("04:00 · 3 services changed (+42 / −5 domains) · 0 rejected", or "not run yet"). The dashboard's headline counts routers in sync ("2 routers in sync"). | ui/README dashboard "Routing". |
| Notifications | `routing.drift_detected` 🟡 "{subject} drifted from what Proxier installed" / "Tags: {tags}. Auto-repair is off: open the router to repair."; `routing.unmanaged_tags_found` 🟡 "{subject} has tags Proxier didn't install" / "{tags}. They stay; adopt, remove or ignore them on the router page." (plural forms where counted). | events.md. |

## Platform change

| Change | Detail |
|---|---|
| `sshx.Target.JumpFirstContact` | The first-contact rule of the jump hop; `Connect` passes it to the jump's `dialHop` instead of `FirstContact`. Tests: a probe target pins the router and refuses an unknown jump host. |

## Go signatures

### `routing/routers` additions

```go
type Registration struct {
	Name   string
	ListID int64 // 0: the default list
	Conn   Connection
}
type Registered struct {
	ID    int64
	Names routeros.Names
}
func (s *Service) Register(ctx context.Context, r Registration, by string) (Registered, error) // store.FieldErrors

type Unmanaged struct {
	Tag       string
	Entries   int
	Names     []routeros.Entry
	FirstSeen time.Time
	LastSeen  time.Time
	Ignored   bool
	Catalog   []string // selectors the catalog offers for it, spelled
	Existing  *services.Item
}
func (s *Service) Unmanaged(ctx context.Context, id int64) ([]Unmanaged, error)
func (s *Service) Adopt(ctx context.Context, id int64, tag, how, actor string) (serviceID int64, err error) // how: v2fly, iplist, existing, custom
func (s *Service) RemoveUnmanaged(ctx context.Context, id int64, tag, actor string) (jobID int64, err error)
func (s *Service) Ignore(ctx context.Context, id int64, tag string, ignore bool, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Repair(ctx context.Context, id int64, actor string) (jobID int64, err error)
func (s *Service) Pause(ctx context.Context, id int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Resume(ctx context.Context, id int64, actor string) error
func (s *Service) Remove(ctx context.Context, id int64, clean bool, actor string) (jobID int64, err error) // jobID 0 when kept
// Drift is pure: the applied tags the router no longer holds as applied.
func Drift(st State, applied map[string]Applied, n routeros.Names) []string

type Hop struct {
	Name   string // "tailnet node proxier", "jump host parents-pi", "router 10.230.2.1"
	Result string // up, off, offline, refused, key-changed, not-tried
	Detail string
}
// Hops is pure: the per-hop table of a connect failure.
func Hops(r Router, s Sync, node tailnet.Status) []Hop
```

### `routing/services` addition

```go
// CreateCustomTx creates a custom service with its rows and first snapshot
// inside the caller's transaction (the caller checked the guard). Adoption
// uses it now, discovery in 3g.
func (s *Service) CreateCustomTx(ctx context.Context, tx *sqlx.Tx, c Custom, rows []DomainRow, actor string) (int64, error)
```

### `sshx` addition

```go
type Target struct {
	Hop
	Jump             *Hop
	Network          Network
	FirstContact     FirstContact // the last hop
	JumpFirstContact FirstContact // the jump hop
}
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `POST /routing/routers/:id/repair` | A sync for drift (repair off) |
| `GET /routing/routers/:id/unmanaged/:tag/adopt`, `POST …/adopt` | Adopt (`how=v2fly\|iplist\|existing\|custom`) |
| `POST /routing/routers/:id/unmanaged/:tag/remove` | Remove from router (strength 2) |
| `POST /routing/routers/:id/unmanaged/:tag/ignore`, `/unignore` | Ignore, stop ignoring |
| `POST /routing/routers/:id/pause`, `/resume` | Pause syncs, resume |
| `GET /routing/routers/:id/remove`, `POST /routing/routers/:id/remove` | Remove (`clean=0\|1`) |
| `POST /routing/routers/:id/remove/keep` | Remove without cleaning (a removing router) |

## Events

Recorded in 3f: `routing.drift_detected`, `routing.unmanaged_tags_found`, `routing.unmanaged_tag_ignored`, `routing.router_paused`, `routing.router_resumed`, `routing.router_removed`; `routing.router_added` and `routing.router_connected` for registered routers.

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/processes/routing/router-sync.md`: the drift check compares type, forwarder and address-list counts too; repair off notifies once per drift set; a drift check that can't connect counts no failure; an awaiting router's own key is pinned by its probe while its jump host must be confirmed; an unadoptable tag (not a valid tag) can only be removed or ignored; ignoring can be undone; removal failures notify at once and leave the router "removing" with Retry and Remove without cleaning.

- `docs/modules/platform.md#ssh`: `JumpFirstContact`.

- `docs/ui/README.md#dashboard`: the Routing area as built.

## As built

Built 2026-10-09 (over two contexts: the usage limit cut the first one after the `routers` code). Every checklist line has its test of that name in that file; `make check`, `make lint` and `docker build .` are green. Every package of the module still runs under `-race`. Headless Chrome wasn't tried (it failed to start in earlier sessions): the pages were exercised through the HTTP tests only.

**Packages** as in Files, except: the pages of 3f are one `pages/routerlife.go` + `routerlife.templ` (bands, per-hop table, the Not Proxier's area, adopt page, remove page, the dashboard body) beside 3e's `routers.go`/`routers.templ`; the texts are in `routing/messages_routerlife.go` (merged by `init`); `TestDashboardRoutingArea` is in the module root's `dashboard_test.go`, `TestDriftAndUnmanagedTexts` in its `notify_test.go`. `services.CreateCustomTx` already existed (3d). CSS for the new parts (`.hops`, `.row.hop`, `.row.unmanaged`, `.row.adopt`, `.choice`, `.area-sub`, `.row.dashrtr`, a sixth column of `.row.rtr`) is in the platform's `app.css`.

**Deviations and additions** (the contract's signatures otherwise hold):

- **Names.** The unmanaged tag type is `routers.UnmanagedTag` (`Unmanaged` is already the plan's action constant); also `UnmanagedOne`, `Adoptable(tag)`, `ErrNoSuchTag`, `ErrInvalidTag`, `ErrNoOffer`, `ErrState`, the `Adopt*` and `State*` constants, `TriggerDrift/Resume/Unmanaged`, `AwaitingFor`, `ProbeEvery`, `DriftEvery`, `Connection.ProbeTarget`, `UnmanagedTags` (pure), `LatestDrift`, `TailnetStatus`, `RemovalJob`. `catalog.Service.Offers(tag)` gives the spelled selectors (`store.V2flyHas`).
- **Hop** is `{Kind, Label, Result, Detail, Via}`: the page words the label ("jump host parents-pi") and the result; results add `unknown` (a first contact not confirmed yet).
- **MakePlan's `RemoveAll`** now removes only the **applied** tags; unmanaged tags stay (3e removed every tag on the router; `TestPlanTable` updated). A sync that removed an asked (unmanaged) tag deletes its unmanaged row after the push.
- **Ignoring** lives with the unmanaged row: while the tag is seen, it stays ignored; a tag that leaves the router loses its row, and coming back is a new set (it notifies again). Stop ignoring adds the tag to the notified set, so it doesn't notify.
- **Drift check** jobs use the syncs' `OnFailed` (only the row is marked failed). With repair on, `drift_detected{repair: true}` is recorded each time drift is found (the repair clears it). `RouterSynced` clears the stored drift.
- **Removal.** Its failures notify when the job gives up (the decision table), not at once (the doc-change line); docs follow the table. An extra route, `POST /routing/routers/:id/remove/retry`, retries the removal job (`jobs.Retry`). Preview is refused (`ErrNotActive`) for a router that isn't active.
- **Awaiting.** The band shows Proxier's public key (the add page has the install commands) and the latest failed probe's error. Router script registrations show "awaiting setup" in the list with "never connected · trying every 10 min until 16 Oct" / "never connected".
- **Dashboard.** There is no global headline, so "2 routers in sync" heads the Routing area (order 40, after Links). Awaiting routers stay listed among the routers needing a look.
- **Phone.** The titleblock's actions (Sync now, Preview, Pause syncs / Resume) and the bands (with the per-hop table and Test connection) come before the stacking columns; no separate "Last known state" area was built: the Tags area (the last plan) is it.
- **Harness.** `routingtest.Registered(name, opts…)` registers a fake router in awaiting setup with nothing pinned.

**Not done / the user's.** No real router, jump host, tailnet or router script: the probe, drift check, adoption and removal ran only against `routerostest`. The pages (bands, Not Proxier's area, adopt and remove pages, dashboard area, phone width) were not opened in a real browser. No Telegram delivery of the two notification texts.
